hints: Halve the coefficient of $x$ to obtain the constant inside the squared bracket, then adjust the remaining constant.
walkthrough:
Complete the square for $x^2 - 4x + 7$:
$$x^2 - 4x + 7 = (x - 2)^2 - 4 + 7 = (x - 2)^2 + 3$$
where $a = -2$ and $b = 3$.

hints: Identify the turning point at $x = 2$, so $f$ is decreasing on $x < 2$.
walkthrough:
The quadratic function $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 3$ has its minimum turning point at $x = 2$.
The function is strictly decreasing on the entire interval $(-\infty, 2]$.
$$\text{Largest value of } k = 2$$

Take square roots, choosing the negative branch because the domain is $x < 1$ ($x - 2 < -1 < 0$):
$$x - 2 = -\sqrt{y - 3} \implies x = 2 - \sqrt{y - 3}$$
$$f^{-1}(x) = 2 - \sqrt{x - 3}$$

Determine the domain of $f^{-1}$ from the range of $f$ on $x < 1$:
$$x < 1 \implies x - 2 < -1 \implies (x - 2)^2 > 1 \implies (x - 2)^2 + 3 > 4$$
$$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: \quad x > 4 \quad (\text{or } (4, \infty))$$

Determine the range of $gf(x)$ on the domain $x < 1$:
$$x < 1 \implies x - 2 < -1 \implies (x - 2)^2 > 1$$
$$(x - 2)^2 + 2 > 3 \implies 0 < \frac{2}{(x - 2)^2 + 2} < \frac{2}{3}$$
$$\text{Range of } gf: \quad 0 < gf(x) < \frac{2}{3} \quad \left(\text{or } \left(0, \frac{2}{3}\right)\right)$$
